As of VASP.6.1.0, each release contains a testsuite for validation.
{{NB|warning|VASP.6.1.0, VASP.6.1.1, and VASP.6.1.2 have a potentially serious issue related to the test suite. Please read about it [[Validation_tests#Known_issues| here]].}}

== Testsuite ==

The VASP testsuite is located in `root/testsuite` where `root` is the
root directory of the build system.

                         vasp.X.X.X (root directory)
                                  |
          ----------------------------------------------
         |              |            |          |       |
        arch           bin       testsuite     build    src
                                     |
                      ------------------------------------------
                     |      |         |         |        |      |
                   tests  README.md  tools   POTCARS  runtest makefile
                     |           
            ------------------   
           |      |           |   
         test1  test2  ...  testN

;testsuite/
: Testsuite root directory. Holds several subdirectories and the main bash-script <code>runtest</code> that runs the tests and validates the results.

;testsuite/tests
: Holds a whole bunch of subdirectories that in turn contain the input files ({{FILE|INCAR}}<tt>.?.*</tt>, {{FILE|KPOINTS}}, and {{FILE|POSCAR}}), and reference output ({{FILE|OUTCAR}}<tt>.ref</tt>, {{FILE|OSZICAR}}<tt>.ref</tt> etc.) for the test calculations.

;testsuite/POTCARS
: Holds the {{FILE|POTCAR}} files (potentials), one for each individual test calculation. The naming convention for these files is:
: <pre>POTCAR.name-of-test-subdirectory</pre>

;testsuite/tools
: Contains a bash-script (<code>call_compare</code>) and a Fortran source file (<tt>compare_numbertable_new.f90</tt>). The latter is compiled as:
: <pre>$(FC) -o compare_numbertable_new compare_numbertable_new.f90</pre>
: where the <code>$(FC)</code> is the Fortran compiler binary path that has to be set in <tt>root/makefile.include</tt> (see the [[Installing_VASP.6.X.X#Compiler_variables | compiler variables section of Installing VASP]]).

;testsuite/runtest
: Main execution script that orchestrates which tests are executed based on set environment variables.

;testsuite/makefile
: Autoconf makefile containing some simple rules that either compile <tt>compare_numbertable_new.f90</tt> (<code>make numbertable</code>), execute a small selection of tests (<code>make test</code>) or execute all test (<code>make test_all</code>).


== Running the tests ==

=== Run the tests with <code>make</code> (recommended) ===
----
After building the <code>vasp_std</code>, <code>vasp_gam</code>, and <code>vasp_ncl</code> executables (e.g. by means of <code>make all</code>), you can test your build by means of:

 make test

(either in <tt>root</tt> or <tt>root/testsuite</tt>).
The above will run a subset of tests from the testsuite (the so-called <tt>FAST</tt> category of tests) that will take roughly 1.5 hours to complete on 4 cores.

The full testsuite may be executed by means of:

 make test_all

The output of the tests (<tt>stdout+stderr</tt>) is written to <tt>root/testsuite/testsuite.log</tt>.

Tests that fail write an <tt>ERROR</tt> to <tt>root/testsuite/testsuite.log</tt> and the tests that were not passed successfully will be listed at the end of this file (and <code>make</code> will exit in error).

To clean up after running the testsuite, execute:

 make cleantest

in <tt>root/testsuite</tt>.


=== Configuring the testsuite manually ===
----
Configured the testsuite by setting several environment variables (with the naming convention: <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_*</code>).

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_EXE_STD</code>:
: The command that runs the standard version of VASP.
: Default:
: <pre>VASP_TESTSUITE_EXE_STD="mpirun -np 4 root/bin/vasp_std"</pre>
: '''N.B.''': Specify the absolute path your ''standard'' executable (e.g. <code>vasp_std</code> or <code>vasp_gpu</code>).

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_EXE_GAM</code>:
: The command that runs the gamma-only version of VASP.
: Default:
: <pre>VASP_TESTSUITE_EXE_GAM="mpirun -np 4 root/bin/vasp_gam"</pre>
: '''N.B.''': Specify the absolute path to your ''gamma-only'' executable (e.g. <code>vasp_gam</code>).

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_EXE_NCL</code>:
: The command that runs the non-collinear version of VASP.
: Default:
: <pre>VASP_TESTSUITE_EXE_NCL="mpirun -np 4 root/bin/vasp_ncl"</pre>
: '''N.B.''': Specify the absolute path to your ''non-collinear'' executable (e.g. <code>vasp_ncl</code> or <code>vasp_gpu_ncl</code>).

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_CUDA</code>:
: Set <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_CUDA=Y</code> to exclude all tests that can not be executed with the CUDA-GPU port of VASP.
: Default:
: <pre>VASP_TESTSUITE_CUDA=</pre>

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_INCAR_PREPEND</code>:
: Additional INCAR tags used for every execution of VASP in the testsuite.
: Default:
: <pre>VASP_TESTSUITE_INCAR_PREPEND=</pre>

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_TESTS</code>:
: Selection of tests to be executed.
: Default:
: <pre>VASP_TESTSUITE_TESTS=</pre>
: '''N.B.''': A convenient way to execute a specific test is to set <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_TESTS</code> to a particular test, e.g. by means of:
: <pre>export VASP_TESTSUITE_TESTS="bulk_GaAs_ACFDT"</pre>
: and to run <code>make test</code> from the <tt>root</tt> or <tt>root/testsuite</tt> directory.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_TESTS</code>:
: Selection of tests to be skipped.
: Default:
: <pre>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_TESTS=</pre>

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_POTENTIALS</code>:
: Path to the POTCAR files.
: Default:
: <pre>VASP_TESTSUITE_POTENTIALS=root/testsuite/POTCARS</pre>


==== Categories ====

A variety of environment variables can be set to run or exclude tests belonging to specific categories.  
Default: not set

For instance:

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_LREAL</code>:
: Skips all tests that use the real space PAW projection scheme ({{TAG|LREAL}}<tt>/=F</tt>) if set to: <tt>Y</tt>, i.e.,
: <pre>export VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_LREAL=Y</pre>

or

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_LREAL</code>:
: Runs only tests that use the real space PAW projection scheme ({{TAG|LREAL}}<tt>=A</tt> or {{TAG|LREAL}}<tt>=.TRUE.</tt>) if set to: <tt>Y</tt>.
: <pre>export VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_LREAL=Y</pre>          

The following variables may be set to skip categories of tests:

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_NOCUDA</code>:
: Skip all tests that can not be excuted with the CUDA-GPU port.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_HYB</code>:
: Skip all hybrid functional tests.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_GAMMA</code>:
: Skip all tests of the gamma-only version.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_NCL</code>:
: Skip all tests of the non-collinear version.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_SOC</code>:
: Skip all tests involving Spin-Orbit Coupling.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_MD</code>:
: Skip all Molecular Dynamics tests.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_TBMD</code>:
: Skip all constrained molecular dynamics tests.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_RPA</code>:
: Skip all tests that involve the Random-Phase Approximation (GW and ACFDT).

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_GW</code>:
: Skip all GW tests.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_ACFDT</code>:
: Skip all ACFDT tests.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_CRPA</code>:
: Skip all tests of the Constrained-RPA.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_BSE</code>:
: Skip all Bethe-Salpeter-Equation tests.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_NOSYM</code>:
: Skip all tests that do not use symmetry.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_LREAL</code>:
: Skip all tests that use the real-space PAW projection scheme.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_LRESP</code>:
: Skip all linear response tests.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_PEAD</code>:
: Skip all tests that use the PEAD method.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_NCORE1</code>:
: Skip all tests that may only be executed with {{TAG|NCORE}}<tt>=1</tt>.

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_SKIP_WAN90</code>:
: Skip all tests that need to execute <code>wannier90</code>.


The following variables may be set to run only tests that belong to a specific category (or categories):

* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_HYB</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_GAMMA</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_NCL</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_SOC</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_MD</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_TBMD</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_RPA</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_GW</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_ACFDT</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_CRPA</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_BSE</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_NOSYM</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_LREAL</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_FAST</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_LRESP</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_PEAD</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_NCORE1</code>
* <code>VASP_TESTSUITE_RUN_WAN90</code>

=== Directly execute the <code>runtest</code> script ===
----
Besides by means of <code>make</code> the testsuite may be invoked by executing
the <tt>root/testsuite/runtest</tt> script directly.
There are two ways to execute the <code>runtest</code> script:

:1. Change into the <tt>root/testsuite</tt> directory and run the tests in the <tt>FAST</tt> category by means of:
: <pre>./runtest -f</pre>
: or ALL tests with
: <pre>./runtest -a</pre>

:2. Change into <tt>root/testsuite</tt>, adapt one of the example configuration files in <tt>root/testsuite</tt> and run the testsuite with:
: <pre>./runtest your-config-file</pre>

'''N.B.I''': To pipe the full output to a file (<tt>testsuite.log</tt>) add <code>> testsuite.log 2>&1</code> to the commands above.

'''N.B.II''': We maintain [[Validation_tests#Configuration_templates | a small collection of configuration templates]].

'''N.B.III''': When you want to run the testsuite by executing the <code>runtest</code> directly you will ''first'' have to build the <code>compare_numbertable_new</code> utility, by means of:

 make numbertable

(in <tt>root/testsuite</tt>).

For each test that fails <code>runtest</code> writes an <tt>ERROR</tt> to <tt>stdout</tt> and the tests that were not passed successfully will be listed at the end of the run.

In case of a successful run, <code>runtest</code> script will exit with error code 0 (indicates successful exit on Unix-based OS), otherwise the error code 1 is returned.


==== Configuration templates ====
The following configuration files are to be seen as templates to help you construct your own:

<u>''General''</u>
* [[All.conf  | all.conf ]]: runs all tests
* [[Fast.conf | fast.conf]]: runs the <tt>FAST</tt> category of tests

<u>''Running with MPI + OpenMP''</u>
* [[Impi+omp.conf | impi+omp.conf]]: for OpenMP + Intel-MPI
* [[Ompi+omp.conf | ompi+omp.conf]]: for OpenMP + OpenMPI

<u>''To test the CUDA-GPU executables''</u>
* [[Cuda.conf | cuda.conf]]

'''N.B.''': these configuration files are sourced by the <code>runtest</code> bash-script. In principle they only set (<tt>export</tt>) some environment variables. Setting these environment variables by hand and invoking <code>make test</code> (or <code>make test_all</code>) amount to the same as running these configuration files with <code>runtest</code>.


== The output of the tests ==

If one runs the tests by means of <code>make</code>, as recommended [[Validation_tests#Run_the_tests_with_make_.28recommended.29 | above]] all output (<tt>stdout+stderr</tt>) will be written to <tt>root/testsuite/testsuite.log</tt>.

Tests that fail write an <tt>ERROR</tt> to <tt>root/testsuite/testsuite.log</tt> and the tests that were not passed successfully will be listed at the end of this file (and <code>make</code> will exit in error).


== What if tests fail ==

We have successfully run the testsuite (on 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8 MPI-ranks) using executables built with [[Toolchains | various toolchains]].

When you run into trouble, ''i.e.'', your testsuite runs report failing tests, we'd ask you to reproduce these errors with one of the aforementioned [[Toolchains | toolchains]] if possible.
If your problems persist with a validated toolchain or you have no access to any of these toolchains, please submit a bug report to the [https://www.vasp.at/forum VASP-forum] and we will look into the matter.

'''N.B.''': This bug report should contain all information we need to try to reproduce the problem: a list of the compilers and libraries you have used to build VASP and the logfile with the <tt>stdout+stderr</tt> output of your testsuite run. 
Please keep the other output ({{FILE|OUTCAR}} files. etc) of your failing tests as well since we might need to inspect these in addition to the logfile in the course of trying to solve your problem.

== Known issues ==

The testsuite scripts in vasp.6.1.0, vasp.6.1.1 and vasp.6.1.2 releases have a potentially serious issue that can lead to loss of user data unrelated
to vasp in the home directory!
This issue has yet been only observed on MacOS and BSD systems, but might affect other OS as well. 
Avoid to use

 make test
 make test_all
 make cleantest

or the use of any script called 

 cleanall 

on MacOS or BSD systems (and potentially other OS) until we release a fix.

This script is used to clean the files produced by VASP after running the test suite.
The <code>readlink</code> and <code>dirname</code> commands take different arguments on Linux and BSD systems including macOS.
On BSD systems this results in the <code>$dir</code> variable becoming empty, <code>cd</code> to the home folder and removing ALL files recursively that do not match the pre-defined patterns.
